title: What things draw, and how long a battery runs them
summary: Typical running watts and start-up surges for common loads, plus plain steps to work out how long a battery will run them. Includes a worked example for a 12 V 100 Ah battery, lead-acid against lithium.

steps.text: Read the label: watts, or volts × amps.
To size an inverter, add the running watts of everything on at once, then the single biggest start surge.
Work out runtime with the steps below, and keep a margin: real batteries give less when cold, old or worked hard.

notes:
## Typical loads
Nameplate watts are the most a load can draw (DOE). Real draw is often lower. Read the label. If it lists only amps, watts = volts x amps (DOE).

| Load | Running | Start surge |
|---|---|---|
| Fridge-freezer | 700 to 750 W nameplate (Generac, DTE). About 70 W averaged over a day (DOE: 588 kWh a year) | 2,200 W in Generac's example. 3 times in DTE's guide |
| Chest freezer | About 25 W averaged (ENERGY STAR: 215 kWh a year) | Plan 3 times (DTE, fridge/freezer) |
| CPAP, built-in humidifier | 53 W typical, 104 W peak (ResMed AirSense 10). Philips DreamStation: 80 W supply | None listed |
| CPAP, no humidifier | No manufacturer figure confirmed. Read the label | None listed |
| Laptop | 50 W (DOE) | 1 times (DTE, computers) |
| Phone charging | 10 W (DR Power). Fast charge: 20 W adapter (Apple) | None listed |
| LED bulb, 800 lumens | 5.9 to 10.5 W (DOE FEMP) | None listed |
| Wi-Fi router | 5.7 W average (NRDC, 2013) | None listed |
| TV, 55 in LED | 110 W typical, 140 W max (Samsung RU7100) | 1 times (DTE, TV) |
| Microwave | 750 to 1,100 W (DOE). Up to 1,500 W (DTE) | 1 times (DTE) |
| Kettle | 1,500 W, 12.5 A at 120 V (KitchenAid KEK1701) | Heating element. DTE lists heaters at 1 times |
| Coffee maker | 900 to 1,200 W (DOE) | 1 times (DTE) |
| Sump pump, 1/2 hp | 1,000 W (DTE) | 3 times, 3,000 W (DTE) |
| Well pump | 1/3 hp 750 W, 1/2 hp 1,000 W (DTE). Deep well 250 to 1,100 W (DOE) | 3 times (DTE) |
| Furnace blower | 1/4 hp 400 W, 1/3 hp 450 W, 1/2 hp 600 W (DTE). DOE: 750 W | 3 times (DTE) |
| Window AC | Watts = BTU/h / CEER. A 12,000 BTU/h unit at CEER 14.7 (ENERGY STAR v5.0 minimum, louvered type) is about 820 W. At CEER 10, about 1,200 W | Plan 2 to 3 times (DR Power: AC needs extra at start. DTE: central AC 3 times) |
| Corded 1/2 in drill | 7 A, 840 W max (Milwaukee 1007-1) | Up to 2 times (DR Power) |
| Circular saw, 7-1/4 in | 15 A, 1,800 W max (DeWalt DWE575) | Up to 2 times (DR Power) |

## Surges and inverter size
- Motors (fridge, freezer, pumps, blower, AC) draw extra for 2 to 3 seconds at start (Generac). DOE puts motor current at about 3 times in the first second.
- Add the running watts of everything on at once. Then add the single biggest start surge (Generac).
- Example: Victron's Phoenix 12/1200 inverter gives 1,000 W continuous at 25 °C and 2,200 W peak. Its peak just covers a 2,200 W fridge start. It cannot run a 1,500 W kettle, which is over its 1,000 W continuous rating.
- At 12 V, a 2,200 W surge is 2,200 / 12 = about 183 A, before losses. Use heavy cable and a proper fuse.
- Start motors one at a time.
- Heating loads (kettle, coffee maker, microwave) have no surge but are big continuous loads.

## Runtime math, step by step
1. **Energy:** watt-hours = volts x amp-hours. A 12 V 100 Ah battery holds 12 x 100 = 1,200 Wh.
2. **Usable share:** lead-acid about 50 %. Lithium (LiFePO4) about 80 %. Victron's own figures use 50 % for AGM and 80 % for lithium. Its lithium cycle life is 2,500 cycles at 80 % depth and 5,000 at 50 %.
3. **Lead-acid loses more under load.** Capacity is rated at 20 hours. At 5 hours an AGM gives 85 %, at 1 hour 65 %. Constant-power inverter loads and cold make it worse (Victron).
4. **Inverter loss:** Victron's 12 V Phoenix inverters peak at 87 to 92 % efficiency, and idle at 4 to 12 W. Plan on 10 to 15 % loss, more at light loads.
5. **Hours** = usable Wh x (1 - loss) / load watts.

**Worked example:** 12 V 100 Ah battery, 60 W AC load, 15 % inverter loss.

| Battery | Usable | After inverter | Runtime at 60 W |
|---|---|---|---|
| Lead-acid, 50 % | 600 Wh | 510 Wh | 8.5 h |
| Lithium, 80 % | 960 Wh | 816 Wh | 13.6 h |

A 12 V load run direct, with no inverter: 600 / 60 = 10 h on lead-acid, 960 / 60 = 16 h on lithium. Battery current is 60 W / 12 V = 5 A direct, or about 5.9 A through the inverter.
